title: Honey Boys, the Della Robia and the family's Exuma and Nassau roots
summary: Local bands and the Della Robia Ballroom, banjo-playing cousin Preston Marshall, and a tangled account of his mother's family and his father's South Carolina ancestry.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now what were some of these bands?
Did you ever have any local bands around there?
Oh yeah. They had the Honey Boys around that time; that was a band that played at the Della Robia Ballroom, and at the time ...
Yeah, the Della Robia Ballroom, and at the time -- and which later became the Rockland Palace.
Oh yeah, that was on Second Avenue, wasn't it?

Second Avenue between 8th and 9th Street. Well, I remember I had another cousin who was still alive in Miami who was a banjo player -- they called him The Ghost. His name was Preston Marshall. Now I have to explain this to you -- in my mother's family, my grandmother came from Exuma.
Exuma -- that's one of the islands in Nassau. And my grandfather was born in Nassau, but he used to travel around the different islands, and that was when he met my grandmother.

And so I have one side of the family as my grandfather's side, and the other side of the family is my grandmother's side. So my cousin Harold is on my grandfather's side, and my cousin Preston is on my grandmother's side, so that's the Exuma side of the family -- and then there's the Nassau side of the family. They're all messed up!

A lot of soul brothers have that kind of thing. I can remember hearing my grandmother say things like that -- "Now this is your cousin Suzie, on your Aunt Mary's side, and this is your cousin Joe on ..." and you really get all mixed up there.

Well, that's the way it went down. Because, you know, I don't know anything about my great grandfather on my grandmother's side, but my great grandfather on my father's side was an ex-slave from South Carolina, and they stole a boat, and that's how they got to Nassau.
Yeah. Actually, the family originated in South Carolina.
